correctness.rationale: For 0<mu<1/2, 0<epsilon<1, 0<=omega<1/2 and zero phase offset, exactly five base points are fixed by the second iterate (one fixed and two primitive two-cycles). Matrix multiplication gives trace 2(cos(2*pi*omega)+epsilon^2*cos(2*pi*mu*sigma_j))/(1-epsilon^2). Monotonicity determines both hyperbolic intervals and the elliptic gap per base cycle. A separate upper-right-entry argument rules out scalar identity at either parabolic boundary; the autonomous fixed-base fiber has no prime-two point for omega<1/2. Thus all full prime-two points are exhausted. The relative ordering has exactly one critical epsilon and a positive analytic crossing slope. The standalone standard-library checker ran successfully with exact rational base enumeration, matrix determinants and traces, circle roots, endpoints, and a 400-case ordering sweep. Finite tests do not replace the proof.

The result reveals a sharp internal reentrant phase diagram: weak forcing has a genuine frequency interval free of primitive two-cycles, while strong forcing has four coexisting cycles across its replacement interval. The critical forcing and signed-width slope classify the complete transition including its parabolic endpoints, rather than a routine isolated threshold or unmotivated slice. No stronger global dynamics are claimed.
